Dated this the 15th day of March, 2024 This is an application for anticipatory bail under Section 438 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 filed by the sole accused in Crime No. 10 of 2024 of Oonnukal Police Station, Ernakulam, registered under Sections 376, 376(2)n, 406, 420 and Section 506 of the Indian Penal Code.

2. The prosecution allegation is that, during the period 30.11.2022 to 28.06.2023, the petitioner committed rape on the de facto complainant on several occasions, and he received amounts from her and later cheated her, by not returning the ..3..
money.

3. Heard learned counsel for the petitioner, learned counsel for the 3rd respondent/de facto complainant, and also learned Public Prosecutor.
4.

Learned counsel for the 3rd respondent/ de facto complainant opposed the bail application stating that the petitioner, who was the owner of the bakery, in which the de facto complainant was a staff, continuously committed rape on her on the promise of marriage, and he had received amounts also from her on that promise.
But later, he committed breach of that promise, and thus cheated her.

5. Learned counsel for the petitioner would submit that the petitioner is a man aged 55 years, having wife and children and the 3rd respondent/de facto complainant also is a lady aged 38 years having her family with husband and children.

So, there ..4..
is no scope for any promise to marry her, and that itself will show the falsity of her claim.

Moreover on 07.01.2024, he had made a police complaint against the 3rd respondent/de facto complainant alleging that, she had committed theft of some amount from his bakery, and for that reason, she was terminated from her job.
Thereafter, she was threatening him over telephone.
The 3 rd respondent/de facto complainant lodged complaint against the petitioner only after lodging police complaint by the petitioner against her.

6. Learned Public Prosecutor, on instructions, submitted that, there was no promise to marry even going by her own statement, and the petitioner arranged a rental accommodation for her and thereafter, forcibly committed rape on her.
7. Going by the records available and the statement of the 3rd respondent/de facto complainant,
prima facie, forcible sexual ..5..

2 intercourse is to be ruled out, especially when the 3 rd respondent filed complaint against the petitioner only after he made a complaint against her.
8.

sentences.text:
In such circumstances, this Court is inclined to allow this bail application on the following terms:-
i.
The petitioner is directed to surrender before the Investigating Officer on or before 25.03.2024, and subject himself for interrogation.
The investigating officer shall interrogate him to collect all materials and evidence relevant for the purpose of investigation including medical examination, if any.
iv. The petitioner shall not try to contact the victim or her family members and shall not cause any kind of harassment to them directly or indirectly.
v. The petitioner shall not influence or intimidate the witnesses or tamper with the investigation.

vi. 
The petitioner has to surrender his passport before the trial court at the time of executing bond and if he is not having a passport, he has to file an affidavit to that effect before the trial court.

vii. The petitioner shall not leave the limits of ..7..
State of Kerala without getting prior sanction from the trial court.
viii. The petitioner shall not commit any offence while on bail.
ix. In case of violation of these conditions, the trial court is empowered to cancel his bail, in accordance with law.
